summary: Frontend-only deep-dive regression on Vesper navigation smoothness vs Kids reference completed on preview URL. Core shelf motion behavior improved and mostly matches expected: single focus invariant held, no post-release queued movement, slot-2 stability observed, trailer request suppression during rapid scrub observed, and WAAPI motion present during normal shelf moves with clean settle. Found remaining mobile/top-nav clipping and a preview-action flow gap under non-playing trailer states.

ui_bugs.issue: Visible clipping/offscreen controls on phone width: left icon/button partially outside viewport and right autoplay button partially outside viewport; fullscreen floating button also renders partially offscreen.

integration_issues.issue: Preview card appears after dwell, but action overlay did not open in tested run because trailer did not reach playing state (actions_count=0). Full overlay->fullscreen->back/resume path therefore not fully validated in this run.
Persistent external addon CORS/502 traffic (plexio/torrentio and cloud-sync warnings) prevents stable network-idle and can cause automation timeouts despite UI being interactive.

issues: Top-nav pill/children exceed effective width and clip visually on both sides
Interactive floating controls near edges reduce touch comfort on narrow screens

action_items: Fix mobile top-nav layout at exact 390x844 so all controls remain fully visible without clipping.
Harden trailer preview action flow when trailer media is unavailable/not yet playing (deterministic fallback or graceful action availability policy).
Optionally isolate/suppress noisy external addon CORS failures during QA flows to avoid false network-idle failures.
critical_code_review_comments: useShelfMotion FLIP path behaves as expected on normal class set (WAAPI running observed during second move, and 0 running animations after settle).

Under simulated .vesper-host-android + .vesper-low-end classes, running WAAPI count was 0 during sample check (then 0 after settle), consistent with aggressive perf-mode animation stripping; verify this is intended on real Android TV hardware.

TopNav currently uses fixed-size icon cells in a centered pill; on narrow mobile widths this can clip edge controls. Consider mobile-specific condensation (fewer icons, horizontal scroll, or compact mode).
seed_data_creation: Used testuser/testpass123 login API and seeded localStorage/sessionStorage: vesper-auth-token-v1, vesper-auth-account-v1, onnowtv-profiles-v1:testuser, onnowtv-active-profile-v1:testuser, vesper-e2e=1, onboarding/whatsnew skip keys. For kids-context regression, seeded onnowtv-kids-config-v1 with a 4-digit pin then opened ?profile=kids.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Kids comparison should be tested via '?profile=kids' context (not '/kids' direct in this environment). Verified kids-home focus movement there. Mobile screenshot after splash removal saved at /app/test_reports/artifacts_iter98/mobile_390x844_home_after_boot.jpg (not listed in links by template rule). Key metrics captured: one focus invariant stayed true, release-state focus stable after 420ms, scrub requests during 8x right @100ms = 0 and after settle = 2, reduced-motion running animations = 0.
rca of the issue: Primary chunky-nav root cause appears resolved by FLIP ownership + scroll arbitration (as provided by E1 context and validated behaviorally here). Remaining user-visible roughness now comes from mobile top-nav clipping and non-deterministic trailer-play state in preview mode. Reproduction: open Home on 390x844 -> observe partially offscreen top-nav edge buttons; focus tile and press Enter after preview appears on a title with unavailable/non-starting trailer -> actions overlay may not appear. Mitigation: responsive top-nav compaction and explicit preview-state fallback/action policy.
